newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shares end down on mining sector correction.
newsitem.headline: Lima shares end down on mining sector correction.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange closed down Wednesday as a technical correction in the mining sector -- soaring recently due to high international metal prices -- dragged the market down, brokers said.
The market was seen dropping again Thursday but buyers were expected to enter the market Friday to arrest the fall, they added.
Wednesday, the General Index fell 0.66 percent to 1,729.10 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index dropped 1.05 percent to 2,487.74 points.
In a total of 1,797 trades, volume was a 45.6 million soles ($17.2 million), according to preliminary figures.
"Basically the mining sector, which has been rising, fell in a technical correction. Investors took profits especially in Morococha," David Alorto of local brokerage Peruval said.
Polymetal miner Morococha, which has gained most in the sector's April bull run, lost heavily Wednesday closing down 8.06 percent to 2.85 soles on volume of 116,000 shares.
